independence_disclosure: This continues my own initially fresh FAQ/history review. I reused my own complete hash-identical source readings and source ledger, not a new fresh vote. The three parent-provided candidate fragments were treated as questions for adjudication, not as supplied authority or another reviewer’s conclusions. No peer review outputs were read.

current_question_verification.current_Q146: Using the classic Filch Wild flare, what items may you illicitly take and from which locations, where may the retrieved ships go, when must the flare be revealed and when may it be zapped, what happens if caught, and what changes about the deck/discards after it is revealed?
current_question_verification.verification_method: Parsed both JSON inputs in script memory and compared complete question objects, preserving order; only Q146 differs. All other literal questions reuse my previous complete reading.

fragment_adjudications.acceptance_scope: Bounded documentary acquisition clause only; the full trigger and full flare are not reconstructed.
fragment_adjudications.operative_quote: Mite Super flare says you “take any cards your opponent discards”
fragment_adjudications.context: The question concerns effects changing a discarded card’s destination before discard, and the answer describes immediate interception/retrieval. Its reward-deck extension is excluded here. The embedded original Mite Super clause does not require a reward deck.
fragment_adjudications.positive_original_base_application: Mite is an original alien; its Super is expressly quoted by the official primary FAQ. Assume only that the acquisition clause is already legally applicable and the opponent is discarding original cosmic-deck cards. This removes the excluded reward-deck branch without assuming the missing trigger, eligible role, phase, cost, quantity of triggering discards, or full encounter-long duration.

actually_asked_overlap.literal_question: For Mite, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when and at what defense hand-size threshold does Bluster act, what two alternatives does defense have, how are cards discarded, and what are ship destinations and encounter status under each choice?

For Vulch, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain whose discarded artifacts trigger Salvage, does played versus unplayed matter, can it salvage its own played artifacts, and what special reveal/retention/new-draw procedure applies when refreshing a hand?
Are discard piles ordinarily public, and may other players inspect every card discarded faceup in a simultaneous group before deciding how to respond?

For Mind Wild, Reserve Wild and Vulch Super, must the flare be replayed for each later qualifying event in that encounter, or does one play last through the encounter? When is Vulch Super first played, and may Vulch collect that same Super through its effect? While Reserve Wild remains active, whose discarded cards of what type may its user take, and where do those cards go?
Can Vulch retrieve the Cosmic Zap that just zapped its power? If another player using Vulch Wild discards artifacts, can an active Vulch retrieve them even if it then has to hand them back again?

fragment_adjudications.why_overlap_does_not_cover: Q047 asks Mite’s sheet power, including how the defense discards, but does not ask Mite Super’s acquisition of those discards. Q066/Q137 concern Vulch artifact salvage, Q123 concerns Reserve reinforcement and Vulch flare acquisition; those card-specific powers do not imply this original Mite Super clause covering any opponent-discarded card within its lawful context. Q083 tests visibility, not card acquisition or changed disposition.
fragment_adjudications.consequential_novelty: The opponent’s eligible discarded cards may be taken under the Super’s acquisition clause. This changes the cards’ disposition and acquiring player’s holdings rather than merely restating public discard visibility or changing a color/count/name in an existing salvage example.
fragment_adjudications.proposed_literal_question: Mite Super’s acquisition clause is already legally applicable, and its opponent is discarding original cosmic-deck cards. Does that clause allow its user to take those discarded cards, and is its quoted acquisition wording limited to a particular card type?
minimal_source_backed_required_facts: The quoted clause allows its user to take any cards its opponent discards within the clause’s legally applicable context.
The quoted acquisition wording itself does not impose a restriction to artifacts, flares, reinforcements, or another individual card type.
facts_not_supplied_or_required: The full activation trigger, role, phase, cost, target restrictions, and duration of Mite Super.
The full Mite Super effect or a claim that every opponent discard at every time is eligible.
An added-to-hand destination that is not written in the quoted clause.
Reward-deck/discard-pile eligibility or later searching of an excluded pile.
fragment_adjudications.own_initial_review_correction: My initial L775 entry rejected the reward-deck question as excluded and treated existing salvage applications as sufficient. That whole-paragraph classification missed the separately quoted original Mite Super acquisition clause. This continuation accepts only that narrower clause; it does not reverse exclusion of the reward-deck extension.
fragment_adjudications.reachable_branch_credit: No independent full-trigger reachability credit is claimed from this fragment alone; the question expressly supplies legal applicability as a condition.

fragment_adjudications.acceptance_scope: The actual procedure described by the official FAQ, without reconstructing missing flare fields.
fragment_adjudications.operative_quote: when playing the Oracle Wild flare, you play the flare faceup in front of you, mix your hands together, get your new hand at random from the mixed cards, and then return the Oracle flare to your hand
fragment_adjudications.positive_original_base_application: Oracle is an original alien and this named Wild procedure uses existing hands and the flare. No Technology, alternate deck, kicker, hazard, or expansion alien is involved. The question starts with otherwise-legal resolution rather than inventing the absent eligibility and activation conditions.

actually_asked_overlap.literal_question: What are the ordinary per-player and per-card flare limits, when does a played flare return to hand, and when does an alien use its own Wild instead of Super?

For Oracle, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when does Foresee act, whose card is played in what manner first, and when does Oracle then select and play its own?
When Machine Wild guarantees a second encounter but the player needs a new hand to take it, what happens to the old hand and to the Machine flare during the replacement?

If a main player’s negotiate loses to attack and that player loses three ships to warp while two allied ships also go there, how much compensation is collected, from where, and what if opponent holds fewer cards?

Using the classic Filch Wild flare, what items may you illicitly take and from which locations, where may the retrieved ships go, when must the flare be revealed and when may it be zapped, what happens if caught, and what changes about the deck/discards after it is revealed?

fragment_adjudications.why_overlap_does_not_cover: Q015 asks when a played flare returns, plus generic limits and Wild/Super choice; it does not ask mixing hands or obtaining a new hand from that mixed pool. Q121 instead asks Machine Wild’s discard-old-hand/draw-new-hand replacement, a different source and procedure. Q050 concerns Oracle’s normal Foresee power and sequencing encounter-card selection, not its Wild. Q011 asks ship-based compensation from the opponent’s existing hand. The updated Q146 concerns illicit Filch retrieval, not hand pooling or random reassignment.
fragment_adjudications.consequential_novelty: Pooling the existing hands and randomly acquiring the new hand from the mixed cards differs from drawing a replacement hand from the cosmic deck or taking compensation from one opponent’s unchanged hand. Holding the flare faceup outside that mixing step ensures the flare returns after that procedure. The acquisition procedure is unasked even though the final generic return rule is already covered.
fragment_adjudications.proposed_literal_question: When otherwise legally resolving the Oracle Wild procedure described in the official FAQ, where is the flare while the hands are mixed, from what cards is the new hand obtained and how, and when does the flare return to its user’s hand?
minimal_source_backed_required_facts: Play the Oracle Wild flare faceup in front of its user.
Obtain the new hand at random from the mixed cards.
Return the Oracle flare to the user’s hand after that effect has finished.
facts_not_supplied_or_required: Which eligible role/phase or trigger permits the play.
The complete flare text, selection of the other participant, numerical new-hand size, or allocation rules not given in this excerpt.
fragment_adjudications.own_initial_review_correction: My initial L525 entry mapped the paragraph only to Q015 and rejected an addition as duplicated return timing. That was too broad: the return-timing component is duplicated, but the expressly described hand-mixing/random-acquisition procedure is a distinct unasked procedure.

fragment_adjudications.acceptance_scope: Only the independent before-card-selection timing clause; no kicker or full Wild effect.
fragment_adjudications.operative_quote: Kickers are played before encounter cards are selected, and so is Loser Wild
fragment_adjudications.positive_original_base_application: Loser is an original alien and the official answer independently places Loser Wild before encounter-card selection. An otherwise legally eligible user can ask whether the flare may be played after cards are already selected without having any kicker in the game. The question assumes legal eligibility rather than specifying an unprovided role, cost, trigger, or full effect.

actually_asked_overlap.literal_question: For Loser, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when is Upset declared, what card-selection restriction follows, how does it change the outcome and when does that reversal happen relative to other effects including zapped Human?
What are the ordinary per-player and per-card flare limits, when does a played flare return to hand, and when does an alien use its own Wild instead of Super?

May the two main players invite one another as allies? Without an exception, may an uninvited other player join, may an invitee refuse, and how many ships from where does each joining ally commit? After alliances, which players select encounter cards, which types are legal, how are they placed/revealed, and when are they normally discarded?
When Loser calls an upset and Pacifist must play negotiate, does Pacifist receive compensation if Loser revealed attack? What if Loser did not reveal attack?

fragment_adjudications.why_overlap_does_not_cover: Q040 asks timing and consequences of the Loser alien sheet’s Upset power. It does not ask timing of the distinct Wild flare, and that sheet timing cannot establish an unrelated Wild effect’s timing. Q015 asks generic flare usage/return/Wild-versus-Super rules, not this card’s selection cutoff. Q152 asks ordinary selection/play/reveal/discard procedure without this preselection permission. Q127 tests Pacifist versus the sheet’s upset and compensation, not Loser Wild.
fragment_adjudications.consequential_novelty: A distinct original flare has an explicit preselection play cutoff. It cannot be derived from generic flare rules or from the separate Loser sheet power. Restricting the question to this cutoff avoids importing kicker return-to-hand behavior or guessing the rest of the flare.
fragment_adjudications.proposed_literal_question: For a player otherwise legally eligible to play Loser Wild, must the flare be played before encounter cards are selected, or may that player wait until after selection?
minimal_source_backed_required_facts: Loser Wild is played before encounter cards are selected; waiting until after selection misses the stated timing.
facts_not_supplied_or_required: Any kicker timing, effect, discard, or return-to-hand rule.
Loser Wild’s full effect, eligible role, exact phase label, activation trigger, costs, or destinations of encounter cards.
fragment_adjudications.own_initial_review_correction: My initial L1528 entry excluded the entire kicker Q/A. That missed its independently stated Loser Wild timing clause, which survives removal of the kicker condition.
